title: After the merge, a walls-only object stops every measurement with an unnamed 'isn't a closed solid' and nothing is highlighted. Round 22's naming now only works when the check is monkeypatched off
detail: The merge points #18's 'flat' handling at term-index's _unenclosed check. That check adds open_solid to why_building, and why_building stops every measurement, so the naming code (unplaced, unplaced_ids, off_named) never runs. What an architect sees: one stray walls-only object (a shed's walls, faces in a line) stops building_area, front_yard, the accessory rows and the height. Each says only 'a building isn't a closed solid' with objects == [], so the panel highlights no object. An off-lot building beside it is not mentioned either. At 2b29efd (#18 before the merge) the same drawing named the object ('a building covers no area seen from above: 1 other building'), said both reasons, gave objects ['shed','wall'], and kept measuring the house's own yards (front_yard 25.0). Round 22's P2 was that the rows 'named nothing'. That is back in the live path. The rewritten test asserts naming only after monkeypatching _unenclosed to return None, and the commit says this naming survives 'as a defence'. But the defence is unreachable: a building whose projection is empty always has zero plan area, so _unenclosed returns open_solid. It only skips buildings that already have problems or no faces, and those set why_building anyway. Views are only built when why_building is empty, so the flat branch in _accessory_yards is dead too. The `how` parameter of off_named is now always 'off'. This is not a false pass (it is stricter), but it is a visible regression of #18's own round-22 fix.
evidence: measure.py:1510-1515: `+ list(dict.fromkeys(why for b in buildings if b.get("faces") and not b.get("problems") for why in [_unenclosed(b)] if why))) or None)` (one generic message, no ids). measure.py:1666: `return "; ".join([stop("open_solid")] * any(place.get(b["id"]) == "flat" for b in bs) + ...` (only reached when why_building is empty, which a flat object prevents). Probe (house 10..35x25..65 0..30, walls-only box 'wall' at 5..15x80..90, box 'shed' at 60..80x25..45, main 'house'): at 66b5c54 building_area, front_yard, accessory_side_yard and building_height each give `None "a building isn't a closed solid" []`. At 2b29efd: building_area `"a building covers no area seen from above: 1 other building ...; a building isn't inside the lot: 1 other building" ['shed','wall']`, front_yard 25.0. test_measure.py:1803-1808: naming is asserted only after `monkeypatch.setattr(mm, "_unenclosed", lambda b: None)`.
pin: packages/model_measurement/tests/test_measure.py::test_a_walls_only_shed_has_one_reason_and_one_off_the_lot_is_still_named. Without the monkeypatch, assert that building_area and every accessory row have 'flat' in objects and say the off-lot shed ('isn't inside the lot: 1 other building'), with 'isn't a closed solid' said once. This must fail against the current measure.py.
suggested_fix: Make measure()'s own open-object reason per object: collect the ids _unenclosed flags and put them in `objects` on every row that waits on why_building (or name them in the stop, e.g. open_solid with {what}). Keep the off-lot reason beside it for the other buildings, as #18's round-22 rule does. Then either delete the unreachable 'flat' branches (place 'flat', unplaced's open_solid term, _accessory_yards' flat block, off_named's `how`) or keep one, with a test that reaches it without monkeypatching.
prior_ref: round 22/23 items (round 22 P2: flat building and off-lot building each named)
skeptics: I could not refute this. I read the code and ran the case myself, and the finding holds. measure.py:1510-1515: why_building now includes the result of _unenclosed(b) for every building that has faces and no problems. measure.py:1312-1315: a walls-only object has no faces that cover any area seen from above (covered is 0), so _unenclosed always returns open_solid for it. That sets why_building, and every measurement then stops with the one generic message. In the placement code at measure.py:1656-1680, the 'flat' place only comes from an empty projection, which always means zero covered area, so the check above has already caught it. Also, building_area adds `objects` only when `not why_building`, so its objects list stays empty. In _accessory_yards (measure.py:2137-2141), the flat branch only runs once views are built, and views are only built when why_building is empty. So the flat-related code that 'names the objects' cannot run in the live path, and off_named is in practice only ever called with 'off'. I ran the test's own fixture (house, walls-only 'flat', off-lot 'offlot') at 66b5c54 using the session .venv with every package on PYTHONPATH. building_area, front_yard, accessory_side_yard and building_height each returned `None "a building isn't a closed solid" []`: no objects to highlight, and nothing said about the off-lot building. The rewritten test (test_measure.py:1800-1808) checks the naming only after monkeypatching _unenclosed to return None. That contradicts the commit message's claim that the off-lot building is 'still named beside it'. The result is stricter and not a false pass, but it is a real, visible loss of round 22's naming in the live path.

I couldn't refute this one; the finding holds. In measure.py:1510-1515 (`_measure`), `why_building` now adds `_unenclosed(b)` for every building that has faces and no problems. `_unenclosed` (measure.py:1307-1323) returns open_solid whenever the area covered from above is <= 1e-6. That is exactly the case of a walls-only object, and also any object whose projection from above is empty, so a "flat" placement can only be reached when `_unenclosed` has been bypassed. As the cited code says, `why_building` stops every downstream measurement, so the per-object naming (the 'flat' / off-lot `off_named` path) never runs in the live code. The test at test_measure.py:1803-1808 asserts the naming only after `monkeypatch.setattr(mm, "_unenclosed", lambda b: None)`, which confirms the defence path is never reached without the monkeypatch. I ran the test's own fixture on 66b5c54 (house 10..35x25..65, walls-only 'flat' at 38..46x70..80, off-lot box 'offlot' at 60..70x70..80) without the monkeypatch. building_area, front_yard, accessory_side_yard and building_height each returned `None "a building isn't a closed solid" []`. No object id is given and the off-lot building is not mentioned. So the panel would highlight nothing, as claimed. I did not run the 2b29efd comparison myself. But the test's own expectations under the monkeypatch (objects ['flat','offlot'] and both reasons) show what the naming would produce if it were reachable. The finding is right that this is not a false pass, since the result is stricter. It is still a real regression in the UX of #18's round-22 fix, brought in by this merge.

title: over_next drops the 'raised room asks' check for every room past x=17 next to a second stack, including rooms clearly above it
detail: 66b5c54 justifies this change by one case: the room can stand inside the second stack (its top meets one of the stack's blocks). The condition `x >= 17 and any(... startswith("s1b"))` is broader than that. It also drops the raised assertion when the second stack is shorter than the room's base, so the room floats above both stacks and is plainly raised. Over the fixed 2,000 seeds there are 159 such rooms: 68 are inside stack 1 and 91 are above it. measure() gives a value for only one of them, an inside case (seed 5, room z 23-30, stack 1 top 40). So 91 drawings lost the raised assertion with no reason given. A regression that stopped asking about a room raised beside or over a neighbouring stack would pass. (Pre-existing, not this branch: in a7557f7 the case the relaxation covers, a room starting at z=23 inside block s1b2 with s1b3 standing on its top, is absorbed into the stack and gets a value. Moved 0.5 ft to z=23.5 it is 'starts above the ground'. That breaks 'moving a part a little never turns one count into another', and belongs to term-index's _stacks.)
evidence: `over_next = x >= 17 and any(s["ids"] and s["ids"][0].startswith("s1b") for s in stacks)` then `"raised": not over_next`. Probe over SEEDS: Counter({'not over_next': 201, 'above s1': 91, 'inside s1': 68}). The only measured value among room drawings: (seed 5, x 17.1, z 23-30, s1top 40, typed 1, value 1).
pin: test_stories_never_take_a_value_below_any_candidate_buildings_floors with the precise condition. Mutate _stories_whole to skip part_raised for parts whose min x >= 17: the precise test must fail (for the 'above s1' drawings).
suggested_fix: Make over_next the room's base below stack 1's top: `over_next = x >= 17 and len(stacks) > 1 and stacks[1]["ids"][0].startswith("s1b") and stacks[1]["height"] > top + dz`. Raise the absorbed-room inconsistency with term-index's _stacks owner rather than relaxing this property.
skeptics: I read packages/model_measurement/tests/test_measure.py:1022-1102 at 66b5c54 and the 66b5c54 diff. Stack k covers x0=5+12k to x0+12, so stack 1 covers x 17-29. The room covers x to x+6 with x in {17.0, 17.1}, and its z starts at top0+dz, with dz in {0.05, 0.5, 3}. The new line 1058, `over_next = x >= 17 and any(... startswith("s1b"))`, sets raised=False whenever stack 1 exists. It does not compare stack 1's height with the room's base. Every stack top is a multiple of 10 and dz is never a multiple of 10, so when stack 1's top is at or below top0, the room floats at least dz above both stacks and is plainly raised. The comment's own justification ("its top may meet one of its blocks") cannot apply there. I ran my own probe over SEEDS with the repo venv: 205 rooms keep the assertion, 94 are above stack 1 with the assertion dropped, and 70 are inside it. My split differs a little from the finding's 91/68 because I classed the boundary case differently, but the substance is the same. measure() gave a stories value for exactly one of these drawings: seed 5, inside, top0 20, s1 top 40, typed 1, value 1, which matches the finding. Today the relaxation hides no failure, since those drawings come back as None. But the check at line 1086, `assert not any(s.get("raised") ...)`, no longer guards about 90 clearly raised rooms, so a regression that gave a value for a room floating above a neighbouring stack would pass this property test. The relaxation is new in 66b5c54; it is not on a7557f7. The note in parentheses (the z=23 vs 23.5 discontinuity) is about term-index code and is pre-existing; I did not verify it, and the main claim does not depend on it.

The finding holds; I could not refute it. I read packages/model_measurement/tests/test_measure.py lines 1032-1066 (_drawing) at 66b5c54, and the diff from a7557f7 confirms that line 1058 is new: `over_next = x >= 17 and any(s["ids"] and s["ids"][0].startswith("s1b") for s in stacks)`, and line 1060 changes `"raised": True` to `"raised": not over_next`.

The comment on the change justifies it only for a room that sits inside the second stack, with its top meeting one of that stack's blocks. The condition is broader than that. It never compares the room's base (top + dz) with the height of stack 1.

The room's base is stack 0's top plus dz, and dz is 0.05, 0.5 or 3. Stack 1's top is always a multiple of 10. So when stack 1 is shorter, the room floats above both stacks with a gap and never rests on anything. It is plainly raised, yet it still loses the raised assertion at line 1083 (`assert not any(s.get("raised") ...)`).

I ran my own probe over the same 2,000 seeds using the repo venv. Results: 205 rooms keep the raised assertion, 94 floating above stack 1 lose it, and 70 inside or touching stack 1 lose it. These are close to the reviewer's 201/91/68; my room detector differs slightly because ids get rewritten in some drawings. measure() gave a stories value for only one room drawing: (seed 5, room z 23-30, stack 1 top 40, value 1). That is an inside case, exactly as claimed.

So in about 90 drawings the room is plainly raised and the property no longer checks it. This is a real weakening of test coverage that this branch introduced. Nothing upstream guarantees the case away and no pattern used elsewhere explains it.

The reviewer's note that a room at z=23 is absorbed into the stack while one at z=23.5 is "starts above the ground" is a pre-existing issue in a7557f7's measure.py, not part of this branch. I did not verify that note independently.

title: Merge left a dead alternative accepting the removed 'isn't drawn as floor blocks' reason
detail: The merge rewrote this assertion as `"isn't drawn as floor blocks" in reason or "could hold up to 4 stories" in reason`. The stories_plain_part stop that produced the first wording was removed in the same merge (stops.py), so that alternative can never match and only hides which reason is expected. The plain stacked garage docstring (line 1274) also still says typed 3 is kept for being 'at least ... the 2 blocks'. That stacked-blocks check (stories_below_blocks) no longer exists.
evidence: test_measure.py:1243 `assert (("isn't drawn as floor blocks" in m["reason"] or "could hold up to 4 stories" in m["reason"]) ...`. grep of packages/apps/docs for `isn't drawn as floor blocks` finds only test text, no stop.
pin: Assert only `"a 32 ft solid (wing) could hold up to 4 stories" in m["reason"]` for typed None. Reintroducing the stories_plain_part wording in place of the bound must then fail.
suggested_fix: Drop the dead alternative. Update the garage docstring to describe the bound rule (typed 3 kept because it is within 3..3: three floors, and an 18 ft garage holds at most 2).
skeptics: I could not refute this. test_measure.py:1243 at 66b5c54 does accept either `"isn't drawn as floor blocks"` or `"could hold up to 4 stories"`. Before the merge, the measurement-2 parent (373f00e^1) produced the first wording: stops.py:71 defined `stories_plain_part`, measure.py:1090 used it, and stops.py:80 and measure.py:1095 did the same for `stories_below_blocks`. At HEAD 66b5c54, `git grep` finds none of `stories_plain_part`, `stories_below_blocks` or `isn't drawn as floor blocks` in any non-test source under packages/ or apps/. So the merge 373f00e removed them, and the first alternative can never match. The only reason left that can match is measure.py:1117 ("a {h} ft solid ({name}) could hold up to ..."). The docstring at test_measure.py:1274-1278 still says typed 3 is "at least the 3 floors and the 2 blocks", which refers to the stacked-blocks check that no longer exists. The same dead wording also appears at test_measure.py:1409, but that branch is never reached with the parametrized z0 values (32.9, 33.05, -0.5). The finding is real and low severity (P3, a dead test alternative and a stale docstring), and it came in with this branch's merge.

I read packages/model_measurement/tests/test_measure.py:1242-1244 at 66b5c54. Line 1243 has the claimed disjunction `"isn't drawn as floor blocks" in m["reason"] or "could hold up to 4 stories" in m["reason"]`, and the diff (diff lines 506-507) shows this branch added it. I searched packages/ and apps/ for "drawn as floor"/"n't drawn" outside tests. The only hits are a docstring at measure.py:1737, a comment at rhino_logic.py:136, the no_stories stop at stops.py:68 ("its stories aren't drawn", which is different wording), and README text. No code produces "isn't drawn as floor blocks", so that alternative can never match. The live reason text "could hold up to N stories" comes from measure.py:1099/1117. The finding also says stories_plain_part and stories_below_blocks no longer exist; a grep for both found nothing in non-test code, so that holds too. The docstring at test_measure.py:1274 ("at least the 3 floors and the 2 blocks") does still describe the removed stacked-blocks reading. The finding is real but cosmetic (P3): a dead branch in an assertion plus a stale docstring, with no wrong behavior.
